value.first: At 6 months he's right on time. I'd go iron-first, then allergens early and often. Health Canada and CPS back it, and the LEAP trial found about 80% less peanut allergy in high-risk babies fed peanut early. Day 1: sit him upright, offer a spoon or two of iron-fortified cereal, puréed meat or mashed lentils. Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, milk continues as usual.
value.second: Week 2, allergens, one new one a day. Peanut first: in the morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter with warm water or milk. Give a taste, wait 10 minutes, feed the rest, watch him two hours, no other new foods that day. Next: well-cooked egg, then yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, thinned nut butters, fish. No allergy testing needed first. Once tolerated, keep each one going about twice a week. Dropping it can raise risk.
value.third: Expect gagging (noisy, red face, normal) and refusal. Choking is silent, so call 911 for that, or for hives, swelling or breathing trouble. A few hives or vomiting after one food: stop it and see your doctor. No honey before 12 months, no whole nuts, no nut butter in a glob. Eczema? Check with your doctor before allergens.
